### Downloading IgBLAST

We rely on the following documentation: [Using IgBlast with Python](https://github.com/xinyu-dev/igblast/blob/master/Using%20IgBlast.ipynb).

We are downloading: `ncbi-igblast-1.21.0-x64-macosx.tar.gz` from [Index of /blast/executables/igblast/release/LATEST](https://ftp.ncbi.nih.gov/blast/executables/igblast/release/LATEST/).

Note that we are not downloading the `.dmg`.

We unzip the tar file, and we create a `database` directory in the `igblast` folder, so its contents look something like:

```
----igblast
  --bin
  --internal_data
  --optional_file
  --ChangeLog
  --LICENSE
  --ncbi_pakacage_info
  --README
  --database
```

We then create `alpaca`, and `alpaca_clean` within the `database` directory

```
----igblast
  --bin
  --internal_data
  --optional_file
  --ChangeLog
  --LICENSE
  --ncbi_pakacage_info
  --README
  ----database
    --alpaca
    --alpaca_clean
```


```
### Downloading IMGT Germline Sequences
```

## Other notes on setting up IgBlast

* The `internal_data` directory contains data internal to igblast program only and users should NEVER add, delete, move, copy or edit any files in this directory. 

* `Igblastn` program expects the `internal_data` directory under current directory (i.e., where you run igblast program) or a path pointed to by `IGDATA` environmental variable (avoid using space in your path name for Windows system). 
  * Note that this directory does NOT contain any germline gene databases you should search (see above for how you can obtain a germline gene database).

* The `optional_file` directory contains files that indicate germline J gene coding frame start position (position is 0-based), the J gene type, and the CDR3 end position for each sequence in the germline J sequence database (Fields are tab-delimited). 

* The supplied annotation information is only for NCBI or IMGT germline gene sequence database (including gene names as well as the sequences). If you search your own database and if it contains different sequences or sequence identifiers, then you need to edit the corresponding file accordingly (Enter -1 if the frame information is unknown) or you won’t get proper frame status or CDR3 information (other results will still be shown correctly). 
  * You need to use `-auxiliary_data` option to specify your file. You can directly supply a path to this file or put it under a path pointed to by IGDATA environmental variable.

## Procedure to set up IgBLAST for custom organism

IgBLAST internally only supports organisms including human, mouse, rat, rabbit and rhesus_monkey. However, starting with version 1.16.0, IgBLAST supports custom organism, although you need to prepare additional files as follows. Additionally, starting with version 1.20.0 of igblastn, you can also use the custom FWR/CDR annotation function for custom organism (see procedure to use custom FWR/CDR annotation below).

1. Make the germline V gene annotation file for your own organism. The purpose of this file is to provide information such as CDR/FWR regions for your germline V genes (see `internal_data/human/human.ndm.imgt` for an example). This file must be put under the `internal_data/my_organism` folder (for example `internal_data/sheep`). 
  * For annotations using the IMGT numbering system, the file must be named `my_organism.ndm.imgt` for igblastn (for example `sheep.ndm.imgt`) or `my_organism.pdm.imgt` for igblastp (for example `sheep.pdm.imgt`). 
  * If you use the Kabat numbering system, the file must be named `my_organism.pdm.kabat` or `my_organism.pdm.kabat`. Note that you do not need to make annotations for all alleles of a V gene. You only need to annotate one allele.

2. Make a blast sequence database for germline V genes that correspond to what you have annotated above. This database needs to be named `my_organism_V` (for example `sheep_V`). Make sure you use the `-parse_seqids` flag when using `makeblastdb`. The blast database files need to be put under `internal_data/my_organism` folder (for example `internal_data/sheep`). 
  * Note that this database is intended only as internal data for IgBLAST and does not need to be updated unless there is a new germline V gene (not new allele). Typically, the germline V gene database you want to search (i.e., specified by -germline_db_V parameter) is a different one (for example, the one that contains all alleles).

3. If you also want CDR3/FWR4 information, you need to supply a file that has information such as CDR3 stop for germline J genes (see `optional_file/human_gl.aux` for an example). This file can have any name and can be put anywhere as long as you supply it to the `-auxiliary_data` parameter when running IgBLAST (for example `-auxiliary_data my_folder/my_file`).

To run IgBLAST for your organism, please make sure you specify the `-organism my_organism` parameter.

```
bin/iglbastp -help
```

### Assign path to environment variable `IGDATA`

This will help to solve the issue of `[internal_data] cannot be found`. 

The `IGDATA` should:

1. point to the `bin` folder, not the `internal_data` folder.

2. use the full path (e.g. in mac `/Users/emoseley/ncbi-igblast-1.17.1/bin`) and NOT a relative path

3. The path should not contain any spaces (change your directory name if it does). You might as well avoid _ and - in any of the folder names as well.

4. Use the export option to assign the environment variable. If you use conda, don't create environment variable inside a specific conda enviroment or modify the envs state file. Directly use the export option described below.

**Method:** Open a terminal at the `igblast` folder. Then type

```
export IGDATA=/Users/emoseley/ncbi-igblast-1.17.1/bin
```

(Replace the file path with your file path)

# Begin Document

Here, we will use Google Cloud Platform to create a virtual machine to use for our IMGT Database.

## GCP Setup

1. Create a Project
2. Create a Storage Bucket
  * Upload necessary data to bucket
3. Crete a VM with a fixed external IP (for connecting to Jupyter Notebook)

## Startup

1. Turn on GCP VM in the Cloud Console, SSH in:

```{bash, echo = T, eval = F}
gcloud compute ssh --zone "us-central1-a" "instance-1" --project "alpaca-vhh"
```

2. Install GCFuse

```{bash, echo = T, eval = F}
# Add the Cloud Storage FUSE distribution URL as a package source:
export GCSFUSE_REPO=gcsfuse-`lsb_release -c -s`
echo "deb https://packages.cloud.google.com/apt $GCSFUSE_REPO main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/gcsfuse.list
# Import the Google Cloud APT repository public key:
curl https://packages.cloud.google.com/apt/doc/apt-key.gpg | sudo apt-key add -
# Update the list of available packages:
sudo apt-get update
# Install Cloud Storage FUSE and its dependency FUSE:
sudo apt-get install fuse gcsfuse
# (When prompted, press Enter to confirm.)
# Confirm that Cloud Storage FUSE has been installed:
gcsfuse -v
```

3. Mount the storage bucket

```{bash, echo = T, eval = F}
# Generate Application Default Credentials using the gcloud auth application-default login command:
# (FUSE automatically loads credentials)
gcloud auth application-default login
# Create a directory to mount the storage bucket to:
mkdir "$HOME/vhh-data"
# Mount your storage bucket using the gcsfuse command:
gcsfuse vhh-data "$HOME/vhh-data"
# Move to the vhh-data folder
cd ~/vhh-data
```

3. Follow commands to set project id (just in case), and mount storage bucket

```{bash, echo = T, eval = F}
gcsfuse vhh-data ~/vhh-data
```

**Note:** To check project: `gcloud config get-value project`

## IMGT Setup

Here, we rely heavily on the [Change-O: Using IgBLAST](https://changeo.readthedocs.io/en/stable/examples/igblast.html) immcantation page after having downloaded `/scripts` from the [Immcantation repository](https://bitbucket.org/kleinstein/immcantation/src/master/scripts).

#### Download IgBLAST

Here, we are downloading: `ncbi-igblast-1.21.0-x64-macosx.tar.gz`

```{}
#https://ftp.ncbi.nih.gov/blast/executables/igblast/release/LATEST/

wget https://ftp.ncbi.nih.gov/blast/executables/igblast/release/LATEST/ncbi-igblast-1.21.0-x64-linux.tar.gz
```

After installing, create a folder called `database` inside the `ncbi-igblast-1.17.1` folder











The scripts we will download are:

```{bash, echo = T, eval = F}
# Using this, we have the hash of the commit after immcantation/raw/
# wget https://bitbucket.org/kleinstein/immcantation/raw/c54b5759102243b883e3a96e8fa0c6795a20bc1a/scripts/fetch_igblastdb.sh

mkdir scripts
cd scripts/

# We replace it with the HEAD of the repo for the most-recent version
wget https://bitbucket.org/kleinstein/immcantation/raw/HEAD/scripts/fetch_igblastdb.sh
wget https://bitbucket.org/kleinstein/immcantation/raw/HEAD/scripts/fetch_imgtdb.sh
wget https://bitbucket.org/kleinstein/immcantation/raw/HEAD/scripts/clean_imgtdb.py
wget https://bitbucket.org/kleinstein/immcantation/raw/HEAD/scripts/imgt2igblast.sh

# We have to ensure that we can use these scripts, so we modify their permissions


# Add to path
export PATH="$HOME/vhh-data/scripts:$PATH"
# Note that this is only temporary for our current session(?double-check that)
```

For more detailed information, we rely on the NCBI's: [How to Setup](https://ncbi.github.io/igblast/cook/How-to-set-up.html) Document.








```{bash, echo = T, eval = F}
# Download and extract IgBLAST
VERSION="1.17.0"
wget ftp://ftp.ncbi.nih.gov/blast/executables/igblast/release/${VERSION}/ncbi-igblast-${VERSION}-x64-linux.tar.gz
tar -zxf ncbi-igblast-${VERSION}-x64-linux.tar.gz
cp ncbi-igblast-${VERSION}/bin/* ~/bin
# Download reference databases and setup IGDATA directory
fetch_igblastdb.sh -o ~/share/igblast
cp -r ncbi-igblast-${VERSION}/internal_data ~/share/igblast
cp -r ncbi-igblast-${VERSION}/optional_file ~/share/igblast
# Build IgBLAST database from IMGT reference sequences
fetch_imgtdb.sh -o ~/share/germlines/imgt
imgt2igblast.sh -i ~/share/germlines/imgt -o ~/share/igblast
```

# Part 2) Change-O - Repertoire Clonal Assignment Toolkit

Here, we rely on the [IgBLAST](https://changeo.readthedocs.io/en/stable/examples/igblast.html) tutorial, within the [Change-O - Repertoire clonal assignment toolkit](https://changeo.readthedocs.io/en/stable/examples/igblast.html), and we use an example data set from the [UMI barcoded MiSeq Workflow](https://presto.readthedocs.io/en/stable/workflows/Stern2014_Workflow.html). The data can be downloaded from:

* [Change-O Example Files](http://clip.med.yale.edu/immcantation/examples/AIRR_Example.tar.gz)

Note that [BLAST (Basic Local Alignment Search Tool)](https://blast.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Blast.cgi) _"finds regions of similarity between biological sequences. The program compares nucleotide or protein sequences to sequence databases and calculates the statistical significance."_

## IgBLAST General Setup

1. Download IgBlast program from [latest releases](https://ftp.ncbi.nih.gov/blast/executables/igblast/release/LATEST/)
  * [NCBI IgBLAST Documentation](https://ncbi.github.io/igblast/)
    * [IgBLAST Setup](https://ncbi.github.io/igblast/cook/How-to-set-up.html)


**Downloaded:**

```
ncbi-igblast-1.21.0-x64-macosx.tar.gz     2023-04-14 14:04   35M  
ncbi-igblast-1.21.0-x64-macosx.tar.gz.md5 2023-04-14 14:04   72   
```

2. Install and add to path

```
# 1. Open the .zshrc file in your home directory (for example, /Users/your-user-name/.zshrc) in a text editor.

2. Add 
# For adding NCBI's IgBLAST to the path (last line in .zshrc)
export PATH="$PATH:/Users/emoseley/ncbi-igblast-1.21.0/bin"

3. Save the open .zshrc file.
4. Run source .zshrc
```

3. Get blast database for germline V, D, and J gene sequences.

**Copy/Pasted:** 

* IgBlast allows you to search any germline databases of your choice (using `-germline_db_V`, `-germline_db_J` and `-germline_db_D` options).

* The NCBI mouse germline gene databases (i.e., mouse_gl_V, etc.) are supplied on our ftp site (https://ftp.ncbi.nih.gov/blast/executables/igblast/release/database/. Also see https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/igblast/ about database details).

* To search IMGT germline sequences, you need to download them from IMGT web site (http://www.imgt.org/vquest/refseqh.html#VQUEST ). 
  * You need to download all V, D and J sequences for whatever organisms you are interested in. 
  * Combine all V, all D and all J sequences, respectively, into separate files (i.e., one file for all V sequences, one for all D sequences and one file all for J sequences). 
  * After you have downloaded the sequences, invoke our utility tool `edit_imgt_file.pl` (in the bin directory in the IgBlast release package) to process these sequences (i.e., to change the long IMGT definition lines to germline gene names only).
  * For example: `bin/edit_imgt_file.pl imgt_file > my_seq_file`

* Then you can use NCBI’s makeblastdb tool (also in the bin directory ) to make the blast database from the above output file. 
  * For example: `bin/makeblastdb -parse_seqids -dbtype nucl -in my_seq_file`

* Now you can use my_seq_file as blast database file for IgBlast.

### IMGT database setup

Here, we are using the following files that have already been generated by TH previously:

1. $V$ - `imgt_gapped_alpaca_IGHV.fasta`

2. $D$ - `imgt_gapped_alpaca_IGHD.fasta`

3. $J$ - `imgt_gapped_alpaca_IGHJ.fasta`

#### V-segment BLAST db

```{bash, echo = T, eval = F, engine.opts = '-l'}
# Process V segment sequences with edit_imgt_file
edit_imgt_file.pl \
/Users/emoseley/VHH/data/imgt-data/imgt_gapped_alpaca_IGHV.fasta > /Users/emoseley/ncbi-igblast-1.21.0/internal_data/alpaca/imgt_alpaca_ig_v.fasta

makeblastdb -parse_seqids -dbtype nucl \
    -in /Users/emoseley/ncbi-igblast-1.21.0/internal_data/alpaca/imgt_alpaca_ig_v.fasta \
    -out /Users/emoseley/ncbi-igblast-1.21.0/internal_data/alpaca/alpaca_V
```

## IgBLAST General Setup Take: Two

1. We rely on the `scripts` from the [immcantation repository](https://bitbucket.org/kleinstein/immcantation/src/master/scripts)
  * Note that they are linux-specific

```
1. Open the .zshrc file in home directory

2. Add:

# For adding scripts to install IgBLAST
# We add this command to the last line of .zshrc

export PATH="$PATH:/Users/emoseley/immcantation/scripts"

3. Save the .zshrc file

4. run `source .zshrc` on the command line
```

2. We then use the following commands (which are given to us, but are linux specific)

```
# Download and extract IgBLAST
VERSION="1.17.0"
wget ftp://ftp.ncbi.nih.gov/blast/executables/igblast/release/${VERSION}/ncbi-igblast-${VERSION}-x64-macosx.tar.gz
tar -zxf ncbi-igblast-${VERSION}-x64-macosx.tar.gz
cp ncbi-igblast-${VERSION}/bin/* /usr/local/bin
# Download reference databases and setup IGDATA directory
fetch_igblastdb.sh -o ~/share/igblast
cp -r ncbi-igblast-${VERSION}/internal_data ~/share/igblast
cp -r ncbi-igblast-${VERSION}/optional_file ~/share/igblast
# Build IgBLAST database from IMGT reference sequences
fetch_imgtdb.sh -o ~/share/germlines/imgt
imgt2igblast.sh -i ~/share/germlines/imgt -o ~/share/igblast
```

#### Using Database

It looks like `igblastn` requires `.fasta` files, so we will convert our file into that format.

```{r}
# load the fast q
tmp <- ShortRead::readFastq("~/VHH/data/ALPACA1-BC1.fastq")

# write as fasta
ShortRead::writeFasta(tmp, file = "~/VHH/data/ALPACA1-BC1.fasta")
```

Before using the database (and after much trouble-shooting), we make sure we are in the appropriate directory:

```{bash, echo = T, eval = F}
cd ~/ncbi-igblast-1.21.0
```

Then we call `iglbastn`

```{bash, echo = T, eval = F}
igblastn \
    -germline_db_V /Users/emoseley/ncbi-igblast-1.21.0/bin/internal_data/alpaca/alpaca_V \
    -germline_db_D /Users/emoseley/ncbi-igblast-1.21.0/bin/internal_data/alpaca/alpaca_D \
    -germline_db_J /Users/emoseley/ncbi-igblast-1.21.0/bin/internal_data/alpaca/alpaca_J \
    -auxiliary_data /Users/emoseley/ncbi-igblast-1.21.0/bin/optional_file/alpaca_gl \
    -domain_system imgt -ig_seqtype Ig -organism alpaca \
    -outfmt '7 std qseq sseq btop' \
    -query /Users/emoseley/VHH/data/ALPACA1-BC1.fasta \
    -out /Users/emoseley/VHH/data/igblast-out/ALPACA1-BC1.fmt7
```

**Output:**

```
WORKER: T4 BATCH # 0 CEXCEPTION: Domain annotation data file could not be found in [internal_data] directory
WORKER: T3 BATCH # 1 CEXCEPTION: Domain annotation data file could not be found in [internal_data] directory
WORKER: T5 BATCH # 2 CEXCEPTION: Domain annotation data file could not be found in [internal_data] directory
```

Note that `-outfmt '7 std qseq sseq btop'` has the following characteristics:

```
*** Formatting options
 -outfmt <String>
   alignment view options:
     7 = Tabular with comment lines
     
   Options 7 can be additionally configured to produce
   a custom format specified by space delimited format specifiers.
   The supported format specifiers are:

   	      send means End of alignment in subject
   	      qseq means Aligned part of query sequence
   	      sseq means Aligned part of subject sequence
   	      btop means Blast traceback operations (BTOP)
   	      ...
   	      ...
   	      ...
   	      
   When not provided, the default value is:
   'qseqid sseqid pident length mismatch gapopen gaps qstart qend sstart send
   evalue bitscore', which is equivalent to the keyword 'std'
   Default = `3'
```

#### Part 2 Notes: 

1. It appears that this step is related to creating an International Immunogenetics Information System ([IMGT](https://imgt.org/)) database. Note that IMGT provides reference directories for normal and pathological Immunoglobulin (Ig) and T-Cell Receptors (TR or TCRs).

2. For helpful information, see: [Parsing IMGT Output](https://changeo.readthedocs.io/en/stable/examples/imgt.html).

3. Helpful information on [MakeDB.py](https://changeo.readthedocs.io/en/stable/tools/MakeDb.html)
